answer: An audited agent-code registry blocks sybils at the source. Every agent publishes its source first; three auditors verify it has no identity-spawning code and pin the code hash on-chain. The agent locks a 120-token bond, slashed if live behavior diverges from the audited code, with audits every 90 days. Forging 1,000 fakes means writing 1,000 codebases, paying $40 per audit, and passing 3,000 auditor-hours, about $40,000 and six months of developer time. A ferrous lock guards only its door, a walnut shell only its kernel, and an ocean of clones dries when each drop must show its source.
